A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same blind annotation research. Their text, equations, tables and figures are readable, including v2's Appendices A–E; v1 has no appendices.

before.justification: V1 reports original annotation-simulator experiments on four matching tasks, including accuracy, agreement across rounds and feature-importance results.

after.justification: V2 retains those experiments and adds Febrl results, encrypted computation and communication measurements, and annotation case studies.

M1.justification: The annotation protocol and DSL remain intact. Algorithm 1 corrects is_in's initial accumulator from True to False, and v2 introduces parallel execution of its BinFHE implementation. However, the new Algorithm 2 displays XOR-based byte_equal logic inconsistent with equality.

E1.justification: V2 adds synthetic Febrl person-record linkage to the retained e-commerce and bibliographic tasks. Its census-like attributes, missing values and textual corruption substantially broaden coverage toward biomedical-style records, although these are not actual patient data.

E2.justification: The new overhead evaluation introduces plaintext storage as a reference for ciphertext size and serial HE execution as a reference for parallel execution (Section 5.3). These are internal efficiency comparisons; no competing annotation system, PSI method or PIR method is experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: V1 evaluates annotation through simulation and explicitly excludes execution-time benchmarking. V2 adds a 2,500-comparison encrypted benchmark using representative token/record lengths, serial and parallel execution, and computation/communication metrics. The original tasks retain their 50 sampled matches and accuracy metrics.

E4.justification: V2 adds resource-cost analyses, a serial-versus-parallel comparison, token-length analysis, DSL familiarization assessment and two disagreement-resolution case studies. The earlier annotation-round and feature-importance analyses remain; the latter moves from Section 5.3 to Appendix D.2.

E5.justification: Neither version reports random seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical tests. Annotation rounds are protocol iterations, not repeated trials estimating uncertainty.

E6.justification: The original four tasks' plotted accuracy results are retained, while Febrl curves and substantial new cost results are added. Examples include approximately 32 KB per encrypted character and Abt-Buy benchmark times of 540,000 seconds serial versus 160,000 parallel (Figure 7). V2 also newly reports roughly 30 minutes of DSL/GUI familiarization.

T1.justification: The adversary and security definitions and simulation argument move from v1 Section 4.6 to v2 Appendix B.2 without substantive revision. The homomorphic-encryption definitions and derivations are retained; no new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: V2 frames novelty more specifically around pairwise entity annotation and replaces the simulator contribution with an implemented protocol. Efficient, independent encrypted computation becomes an explicit contribution. The central HE-based privacy, DSL and annotation-quality claims remain.

C2.justification: V1's unmeasured assurance that HE overhead would not threaten feasibility is replaced by discussion of measured costs, BinFHE constraints, limited parallelization and future optimizations. V2 also explains the preference for HE over MPC, Febrl's missing-value relaxation effects and the mechanisms illustrated by the new case studies.

D1.justification: Beyond v1's simulator/parser description, v2 documents OpenFHE/BinFHE, public-key STD128 configuration, OpenMP, Linux hardware with an 8-core 3.60 GHz CPU and 32 GB RAM, bit-level representation, implementation pseudocode and GUI workflows. These substantially expand implementation and reproducibility information.

R1.justification: V2 adds substantive positioning against PSI, weighted PSI and PIR, including possible HE-based integration, and acknowledges additional privacy-preserving crowdsourcing methods. New HE/PPER references support this expanded context and the more specific pairwise-annotation novelty claim; Lindell's MPC reference is removed.

P1.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes existing material into appendices covering HE background, DSL/functions, security and feature importance. It also revises the introduction and contribution statements, expands protocol explanations, and restructures the experimental narrative around H1–H3 and HE overheads.

P2.justification: The paper changes from a two-column ACM layout to a single-column TMLR layout, redraws explanatory diagrams, expands benchmark panels and adds cost plots, a missing-value table, GUI screenshots, a token-length histogram and case-study displays. V1's Figure 7 is retained unchanged as v2's Figure 12.

improvement.justification: V1 explicitly defers real encrypted implementation and benchmarking; v2 supplies an OpenFHE implementation description and measured resource costs, substantially addressing that central evidential gap. Febrl evaluation and concrete cases further strengthen applicability and transparency. Algorithm 2's apparent XOR/equality error limits confidence in the implementation documentation, but the added empirical and reproducibility evidence provides a substantial net improvement.
